messages:
lina: Quick note for this week's release train: we're tightening slow-canary rollback rules after last sprint's regressions.
raj: TL;DR of the change?
lina: Canary will now have a slower ramp and two automated safety checks. Sequence: 1% -> 8% -> 30% -> 100% with 15m observation at each step.
release-lead: Automated safety checks = (a) latency p95 > 320ms for 5m OR (b) error_rate increase >0.6% sustained for 3m. Either triggers auto-abort.
sre-oncall: We'll add a secondary check for route-lookup-hitratio drop >10% as an early signal. If that fires, we mark the canary as "investigate" and page.
raj: Any change to who can approve manual aborts?
lina: Manual abort still requires release lead + oncall ack. Auto-abort bypasses manual approval and triggers incident creation.
ops-bot: Deploy dry-run scheduled: 2025-08-15T02:00:00Z. Dry-run will validate auto-abort hooks only.
release-lead: Reminder: update your changelogs with a one-line note if you include infra-affecting changes. This helps post-deploy triage.
sre-oncall: I'll push a short dashboard with the new thresholds and an alert playbook; link will be posted here.
raj: Sounds good. Will we backfill any retro notes from the last incident?
lina: Yes, short retro posted: "canary cadence too aggressive; insufficient early signals" -> changed cadence + route-lookup check.
release-lead: OK team, soft freeze at 2025-08-14T23:30:00Z for the train. Keep non-critical merges on hold. Tag this thread id 2023456789 for follow-ups.
sre-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll monitor and report status during rollout.
ops-bot: Canary policy updated in infra docs: https://confluence.redwood/infra/canary-policy (internal).
